newsitem.title: USA: New products for summer safety and entertainment.
newsitem.headline: New products for summer safety and entertainment.

text.p: Just as America's drivers are taking to the road for summer vacations, Reader's Digest has come out with a new book designed to help avoid some of the season's most vexing problems -- car repairs.
"The Family Handyman -- Simple Car Care and Repair," is an illustrated guide to simply and safely making needed repairs to your car.

From identifying leaks to fixing lights and blinkers, the book takes an under-the-hood look at keeping your car running smoothly without costly trips to the mechanic for something you can easily do yourself.

When all else fails, the book also gives handy advice about choosing a mechanic and understanding some of the mechanic's lingo. For example, when the mechanic says, "Your caliper's stuck ..." he means, "your brakes are totally shot."
The hardcover, spiral-bound book opens and stays flat, so it can be referred to while adjusting your newly charged battery.
The book, being distributed this month, sells for $19.95. It can be purchased from Reader's Digest by calling 1-800-788-6262. Or, you can contact the web site: http://www.readersdigest.com.
Itching -- it's nothing new. Lanacane, makers of anti-itch products, has come out with two new products to address the up to 30 different kinds of itches one can have.
The new preparations, available over-the-counter, join the $200 million anti-itch (anti-pruritic) category.

One new product, just reaching stores now, is Maximum Strength Lanacane anti-itch creme medication. It has three times the itch and pain-fighting medicine to relieve intense, burning itch, Lanacane said. It sells for $4.44 for a one-ounce container.
A second new product is Lanacane Anti-itch creme medication with "potent antibacterial." It helps prevent infection that can result from scratching. It sells for $3.97 for a one-ounce container.

Another handy statistic. Ninety percent of the U.S. population is sensitive to poison ivy, oak or sumac. Reactions to these toxins account for the greatest proportion of worker's compensation payments related to outdoor injuries, according to a study by the University of Delaware and commissioned by Lanacane.
To receive a free pamphlet, "A guide to summer itching," about insect stings, poisonous plants and other itch producers, write to: Lanacane, PO Box 328-LC, White Plains, N.Y. 10602-0328.
MGM Studios plans to unveil new licensing deals featuring its famed 30-year old character, the Pink Panther.

The studio is holding its products under wraps until the upcoming 1997 International Licensing Show to be held in New York, but said products will feature "a colourful and hip new logo" and "fun fashion designs for adults and children."
MGM will also show off its plans to license characters and images from the television series "Stargate SG-1," "Fame LA," "All Dogs Go To Heaven" and "The Outer Limits."
"Stargate SG-1," from MGM Television, is scheduled to begin broadcasting this summer on Showtime Network. The show, based on the 1994 movie "Stargate," will have a new fantastic story each week.
"Fame LA," a weekly one-hour drama, will debut in the fall.

Scholastic Productions will be licensing new products related to the PBS programme, "The Magic School Bus," "Clifford the Big Red Dog" books, and the new "Anamorphs," the book series written by K.A. Applegate.

Auto racing is not new to licensing. Mattel has set up a new licensing programme for products tied to the No. 44 Hot Wheels Pontiac Grand Prix, the car driven by Kyle Petty in the NASCAR Winston Cup Series, which is being held all over the country and runs through November.
Hot Wheels, Mattel's $250 million brand of die-cast toy cars, playsets and tracks, will be promoting products that twin Petty with the Hot Wheels name.
New products include apparel for children and adults, trading cards, posters, flags and pennants and collectible plates.
They are being introduced into stores now and at race tracks where the Winston Cup Series races are being held.

Close-Up Toothpaste is teaming up with NASCAR driver Jeff Gordon and producing packages that feature a series of collectible photos of the driver. Each limited edition package, available in six-ounce Classic Red gel, Tartar Control Mint gel and Mint toothpaste with baking soda, will sell for a suggested retail price of 99 cents.
The collectible packages will be available through the end of the year.
The National Plastics Council has published several new brochures on food safety and nutrition. Both are free.

"Food Safety: Practical, Easy Steps You Can Take to Help Keep Your Family Safe" includes nine steps to safe food handling and storage, cooler tips for safer picnicking, and turkey traps and tips for cooking holiday meals.
"Refrigerator Makeover Guide" has easy-to-follow storage tips designed to keep foods fresher and preserve nutrients, prevent spoilage and stretch grocery dollars.
To receive both brochures, call 1-800-2-HELP-90 (243-5790).
